tasks.prompt: Inputs are integers. Reject any input outside 0..255 by returning -1. Write align_up(value: int, alignment: int) -> int. Also reject alignment zero or alignment not a power of two. Return the smallest multiple of alignment at least value, or -1 if the result exceeds 255.

Inputs are integers. Reject any input outside 0..65535 by returning -1. Write align_up(value: int, alignment: int) -> int. Also reject alignment zero or alignment not a power of two. Return the smallest multiple of alignment at least value, or -1 if the result exceeds 65535.

Inputs are integers. Reject any input outside 0..255 by returning -1. Write overlap_size(a_start: int, a_end: int, b_start: int, b_end: int) -> int. Reject an end smaller than its start. Return the number of integer positions in the intersection of half-open intervals [a_start,a_end) and [b_start,b_end). Empty intervals and touching endpoints have zero overlap.

Inputs are integers. Reject any input outside 0..255 by returning -1. Write ring_distance(start: int, end: int, modulus: int) -> int. Also reject modulus zero or either position at least modulus. Return the forward distance from start to end wrapping at modulus; equal positions have distance zero.

common_instruction: Return only one Python function, with no Markdown fences or explanatory prose. Use integer/bool literals, local assignment, if/else, return, comparisons, and/or/not, conditional expressions, +, -, *, //, %, and bitwise & only. No calls (including min/max), imports, loops, shifts, exponentiation, decorators, helper functions, containers or strings. Keep the source under 4096 bytes. These are local Python reference tasks, not native OS validation.
